x: Jack Brown went next for us and he ran a well-judged race to catch the Walton man down the home straight, but Len Herbert could not hold Nankeville over the final leg, and we finished second in 17 min. 25 secs., which was only just outside the British (National) record of 17 min. 22.6 secs.

It was interesting to note that Nankeville only did 18.43. Our total time of 3.53.44 would have won the race on previous occasions, so it was not a question of our chaps failing, but of the other clubs improving.

"Jock" Cameron was 2nd in 51.2 secs., and Jack Brown won the 880, with Frank Wright in 2nd place in 1 min. 59.4 secs. Peter Bagnall was 2nd to Nankeville in a 4 mins. 15 secs 1 mile. and Chas. Walker won the 3 miles in 14 mins. 46.4 secs.
Wes Santee, America's hot favourite for that honour, was entered together with Chataway and Nankeville plus Lawrenz (Germany) and Ericsson (Sweden).
